{
  "analyses": [
    {
      "paper_id": "2608.13237",
      "title": "When Should Multi-Round RAG Stop? Structured Stopping Judgments and Retrieval Reduction in Search-R1",
      "research_question": "Can a structured sufficiency-and-gap judge change only the stopping time of a frozen multi-round Search-R1 trajectory to reduce retrieval while keeping answer-quality loss within a prespecified bound, and what stopping risk remains?",
      "methodology": "The study freezes Search-R1's reasoner, E5 top-3 retriever, Wiki-2018 corpus, prompt, and four-search budget, then constructs reachable retrieval states and labels whether a correct answer is already recoverable using a frozen answer-only probe. It trains a Qwen3.5-2B structured judge on 3,009 states from 900 disjoint HotpotQA training questions and selects its stopping threshold on grouped validation under a STOP-precision constraint. A held-out 800-question confirmatory evaluation applies the first threshold crossing on each trajectory and measures exact match, search calls, state-ranking quality, calibration, and safe versus unsafe early stops with paired bootstrap confidence intervals.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The confirmatory stopping policy removed 77 retrieval calls, reducing mean searches from 2.60125 to 2.50500, a 3.70% reduction, with the confidence interval satisfying the prespecified retrieval-reduction criterion.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Confirmatory Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Official exact match decreased from 0.44875 to 0.44250, a 0.625 percentage-point loss whose confidence interval remained inside the prespecified two-percentage-point noninferiority margin; this does not establish unchanged or improved accuracy.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Confirmatory Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Among 69 confirmatory early stops, 42 were classified as safe and 27 as unsafe, so 39.13% of the executed early stops were unsafe under the paper's probe-based definition.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Risk Diagnostics"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The expanded structured judge improved STOP average precision over the structured-base judge, but validation STOP precision did not transfer to the final test set and calibration remained weak.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Confirmatory Results and Risk Diagnostics"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Exploratory trajectories contained substantial over-retrieval headroom: 143 of 523 native SEARCH actions occurred after the answer probe was already correct, and a native-preserving cost oracle could remove 131 searches while retaining native exact match.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Exploratory Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Reducing retrieval calls is not equivalent to reducing total system cost because the additional judge introduces compute, memory, and latency that were not included in the retrieval-call metric.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Discussion"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The conclusions are conditional on a frozen Search-R1 configuration and a HotpotQA-based evaluation rather than a broad set of RAG systems and domains.",
        "The learned stopping policy is not risk-certified: a substantial fraction of executed early stops were unsafe under the paper's own probe-based criterion.",
        "The high validation STOP precision was based on a small number of positive stop predictions and did not transfer to the confirmatory set.",
        "The evaluation counts retrieval calls but does not normalize end-to-end latency, token usage, memory, or judge-computation cost.",
        "The correctness labels rely on a frozen answer-only probe, so they operationalize recoverability rather than proving that the retrieved evidence is complete or sufficient in a stronger semantic sense.",
        "Per-question trajectories, benchmark-derived labels, and model weights are not redistributed in the reproduction repository, although the underlying benchmark and upstream resources remain available under their original licenses."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "retrieval_reduction": 0.99,
        "accuracy_within_prespecified_margin": 0.99,
        "unsafe_stopping_risk": 0.99,
        "ranking_policy_mismatch": 0.96,
        "over_retrieval_headroom": 0.98,
        "total_cost_not_established": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "The paper treats multi-round RAG stopping as a sequential decision over already reachable reasoning and retrieval states.",
        "A frozen answer-only probe is used to decide whether an official answer is already recoverable at a state.",
        "The structured judge predicts sufficiency and evidence gaps without changing the underlying Search-R1 reasoner or retriever.",
        "The judge was trained on 3,009 clean states derived from 900 HotpotQA training questions.",
        "The confirmatory evaluation contains 800 held-out HotpotQA questions.",
        "The learned policy reduced mean search calls by 0.09625 per question.",
        "Official exact match fell by 0.00625 in absolute proportion.",
        "Only a minority of available safe early-stop opportunities were actually captured by the learned policy.",
        "Validation precision substantially overestimated confirmatory STOP precision.",
        "The paper explicitly cautions that fewer searches do not by themselves demonstrate lower total inference cost."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13237",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-18653-v1-2026-findings-acl-2090",
      "title": "Beyond Single-Shot: Multi-step Tool Retrieval via Query Planning",
      "research_question": "Can iterative query planning that decomposes complex requests and adapts subsequent queries to retrieval feedback outperform single-shot retrieval for large compositional tool libraries and improve downstream tool execution?",
      "methodology": "ToolQP first produces a natural-language plan that decomposes an instruction into retrieval-relevant subtasks, then iteratively generates queries while conditioning on previous retrieval feedback and aggregates tools using their best rank across attempts. Because standard tool-retrieval datasets lack query trajectories, the authors synthesize training trajectories with a teacher model, including successful and selected failed-then-corrected query attempts, and use them for supervised fine-tuning. The model is subsequently optimized with GRPO-style reinforcement learning with verifiable retrieval rewards based on final nDCG and recall/completeness, plus formatting and plan-semantic constraints. Evaluation uses ToolRet across Web, Code, and Custom tool collections, transfer to retrievers not used for trajectory generation, ablations, and end-to-end execution on API-Bank and StableToolBench.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "On ToolRet, ToolQP improved the reported macro zero-shot nDCG@10 and Completeness@10 from 29.8 and 27.0 for the base gte-Qwen retriever to 36.9 and 35.8.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "When transferred to retrievers not used to create its training trajectories, ToolQP produced average zero-shot gains of 5.4 points in nDCG@10 and 7.1 points in Completeness@10.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Retriever Transfer"
        },
        {
          "finding": "End-to-end evaluation showed higher execution performance after ToolQP retrieval, including about a three-point accuracy improvement on API-Bank and roughly eight-to-nine-point pass-rate improvements on the reported StableToolBench measures.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "End-to-End Evaluation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Ablations indicate that supervised training supplies most of the in-domain improvement, while the subsequent reinforcement-learning stage provides additional gains and is particularly useful for zero-shot performance.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Ablation Study"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Removing the original user instruction from the iterative planner reduced performance, supporting the use of the original request as an anchor when subtask decomposition or intermediate retrieval feedback is incomplete.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Ablation Study"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Qualitative examples show that feedback-conditioned retrieval can expose an implicit prerequisite tool that was not explicitly named in the original request, although this evidence is illustrative rather than a quantified dependency-recovery evaluation.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Qualitative Analysis"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Synthetic query trajectories were generated against a single base retriever, which the authors note can bias the planner toward that retriever's embedding and ranking behavior.",
        "Inter-tool dependencies are handled implicitly through iterative retrieval interaction; the paper notes that explicit tool knowledge graphs could represent such dependencies more efficiently.",
        "The training supervision is synthetic and therefore inherits errors and assumptions from the teacher-generated plans, subtasks, and candidate queries.",
        "The experiments focus on tool discovery and execution benchmarks rather than document evidence retrieval with permission, version, or temporal-validity constraints.",
        "The stopping condition is based on subtask coverage within the query-planning procedure rather than a calibrated guarantee that all decision-relevant evidence has been found.",
        "The paper does not provide an end-to-end cost model balancing additional planning/model inference against retrieval savings."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "toolret_zero_shot_improvement": 0.99,
        "cross_retriever_transfer": 0.98,
        "downstream_execution_improvement": 0.97,
        "sft_and_rlvr_contributions": 0.96,
        "original_query_anchoring": 0.97,
        "implicit_dependency_discovery": 0.86
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "ToolQP represents retrieval as an iterative query-planning process instead of one embedding lookup for the whole request.",
        "The planner decomposes a complex instruction into subtasks before interacting repeatedly with a retriever.",
        "Later queries are conditioned on feedback from earlier retrieval attempts.",
        "The final tool ranking uses the best rank achieved by each tool across multiple retrieval attempts.",
        "The training trajectories are synthetically generated because existing tool-retrieval datasets do not provide multi-step query trajectories.",
        "The training data includes some failed retrieval attempts followed by successful revisions so that the model can learn correction behavior.",
        "Reinforcement learning optimizes sequence-level retrieval measures over the aggregated final tool list.",
        "ToolQP was trained with trajectories produced using one retriever but was evaluated with several different retrievers.",
        "Keeping the original user request in the planner context improves retrieval relative to relying only on its decomposition.",
        "The authors identify explicit modeling of inter-tool dependencies as an avenue for further improvement."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2601.07782",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2604.25676",
      "title": "CORAL: Adaptive Retrieval Loop for Culturally-Aligned Multilingual RAG",
      "research_question": "Can critique-driven iterative revision of both the corpus selection and the retrieval query improve culturally aligned multilingual RAG compared with fixed multilingual retrieval spaces?",
      "methodology": "CORAL uses a planner to select language-specific corpora and formulate retrieval queries and a critic to score retrieved documents for relevance, usefulness, specificity, and contextual compatibility, then decide whether accumulated evidence is sufficient. Each selected corpus contributes top-ranked documents, validated documents accumulate across iterations, and an insufficient or culturally misaligned evidence set triggers feedback to the planner for corpus reselection and query reformulation; the highest-scoring validated documents are ultimately passed to the answer generator. Experiments use BLEnD and CLIcK cultural question answering, 13 language-specific Wikipedia corpora from October 2025, two large planner/critic backbones, multiple answer generators, fixed-scope and multilingual-RAG baselines, and component ablations.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "CORAL achieved the strongest reported accuracy across the evaluated resource tiers and planner/critic configurations, with the final paper reporting improvements of roughly four percentage points on low-resource BLEnD averages in one configuration and up to 2.82 points on CLIcK.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "For the Qwen-based planner and critic, dynamic corpus selection without query rewriting improved the reported BLEnD mid-resource score by 3.78 points and CLIcK by 6.62 points relative to the multiRAG baseline.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Ablation Study"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Adding query reformulation on top of dynamic selection produced further gains; with the GPT-OSS configuration the reported increments included 2.36 points on low-resource BLEnD and 1.41 points on CLIcK.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Ablation Study"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Fixed retrieval from a culture's own language corpus remained below CORAL in the reported ablation, while indiscriminately pooling corpora could introduce culturally mismatched evidence.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Static Corpus Ablation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "In a manual analysis of 158 rewritten queries from 100 CLIcK questions, 53.8% of rewrites narrowed the query and 32.9% were categorized as paraphrases; narrowing frequently supplied contextual details that the critic had identified as missing.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Query Reformulation Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "CORAL contains an explicit evidence-sufficiency feedback loop and can terminate early, but the paper also acknowledges that this additional agentic reasoning incurs inference cost and calls for future cost-aware stopping methods.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Method and Limitations"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The retrieval collection is restricted to language-specific Wikipedia corpora, so culturally relevant knowledge that is absent or sparse in Wikipedia cannot be recovered by the loop.",
        "Wikipedia coverage varies substantially across languages and can privilege well-documented perspectives while underrepresenting others.",
        "The main evaluation uses multiple-choice cultural question answering and therefore does not test many open-ended or multi-turn failure modes.",
        "The language and corpus set was restricted for computational reasons and does not cover arbitrary multilingual or regional information sources.",
        "Agentic corpus selection, criticism, and query reformulation increase inference cost even though the system uses iteration limits and early termination.",
        "The paper discusses privacy and access-control requirements for deployment with sensitive or private sources, but these permission-enforcement mechanisms are not part of the evaluated retrieval loop.",
        "The experimental design does not explicitly model document versions, superseded evidence, or temporal-validity checks."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "adaptive_retrieval_improves_accuracy": 0.97,
        "dynamic_corpus_selection_contribution": 0.99,
        "query_rewriting_contribution": 0.98,
        "fixed_scope_limitation": 0.97,
        "rewrite_behavior_analysis": 0.99,
        "agentic_cost_tradeoff": 0.97
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "CORAL adapts both the retrieval corpus and the retrieval query in response to the quality of currently retrieved evidence.",
        "A planner chooses retrieval corpora and queries while a separate critic evaluates retrieved evidence.",
        "The critic scores documents along four dimensions before accepting them as validated evidence.",
        "Documents that pass the validation thresholds can accumulate across retrieval iterations.",
        "Insufficient evidence causes the critic's feedback to be sent back to the planner for another retrieval attempt.",
        "The final generator receives a small set of the highest-scoring validated documents.",
        "Dynamic corpus selection contributes substantial gains over a fixed multilingual retrieval setup in the reported ablations.",
        "Query reformulation supplies additional gains beyond dynamic corpus selection alone.",
        "Manual analysis indicates that many query rewrites narrow retrieval by adding missing contextual cues.",
        "The authors state that real deployments over sensitive material require privacy and access-control mechanisms beyond the experimental setup."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1356.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2212.10509",
      "title": "Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions",
      "research_question": "Does repeatedly alternating chain-of-thought reasoning with retrieval, so that each reasoning step can determine what evidence to retrieve next, improve evidence recall and answer quality on knowledge-intensive multi-step questions?",
      "methodology": "IRCoT starts with passages retrieved for the original question, generates one chain-of-thought sentence from the question, accumulated evidence, and prior reasoning, then uses that new reasoning sentence as the query for another retrieval step. This reason-retrieve cycle terminates when the generated reasoning contains an answer marker or after a maximum of eight iterations, while limiting the accumulated evidence set to 15 paragraphs. The authors evaluate GPT-3 and multiple Flan-T5 sizes with BM25 retrieval on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC, measuring fixed-budget retrieval recall and downstream QA F1 and exact match, with additional out-of-domain, model-scale, and factuality analyses.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "With GPT-3 as the reasoning model, IRCoT increased fixed-budget retrieval recall over one-step retrieval by 11.3, 22.6, 12.5, and 21.2 points on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC respectively.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Retrieval Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Interleaved retrieval also improved downstream QA F1 on most evaluated settings, including gains of 7.1, 13.2, and 7.1 points with GPT-3 on the first three datasets, although the large IIRC retrieval gain did not yield a corresponding QA improvement.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Question Answering Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "IRCoT retained retrieval and QA advantages under cross-dataset demonstrations in the reported out-of-domain experiments, except that IIRC was excluded from this comparison because of its different structure.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Out-of-Domain Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Manual factuality analysis found fewer factual errors in IRCoT reasoning than in the one-retrieval baseline, including reported reductions of 50% on HotpotQA and 40% on 2WikiMultihopQA.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Factuality Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Retrieval improvements appeared across all tested language-model sizes, including small Flan-T5 models, whereas downstream QA gains were less reliable at the smallest scale.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Model Scale Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The method's stopping mechanism is a generated answer-marker heuristic plus a hard iteration cap rather than an independently calibrated assessment that the accumulated evidence is sufficient.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Method"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The method relies on a language model being able to generate useful zero-shot or few-shot chain-of-thought reasoning, which the authors report as more difficult for smaller models.",
        "Interleaving many retrieved paragraphs with demonstrations and prior reasoning requires a relatively long model context window.",
        "The GPT-3 code-davinci-002 model used in the experiments was deprecated after submission, making exact reproduction of those results difficult.",
        "Stopping is based on the model producing an answer marker or reaching an eight-step cap rather than on calibrated evidence completeness, uncertainty, or retrieval value.",
        "The system does not explicitly enforce permissions, source versions, provenance freshness, or temporal validity.",
        "The evaluation bounds retrieval by paragraph count but does not optimize a comprehensive end-to-end cost function covering reasoning-model inference and retrieval."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "retrieval_recall_improvement": 0.99,
        "qa_improvement": 0.98,
        "out_of_domain_robustness": 0.94,
        "factual_error_reduction": 0.96,
        "model_scale_effect": 0.96,
        "heuristic_stopping": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "IRCoT alternates one reasoning step with one retrieval step instead of retrieving all supporting evidence before reasoning.",
        "Each newly generated chain-of-thought sentence becomes the basis for the next retrieval query.",
        "Retrieved paragraphs accumulate so later reasoning has access to evidence obtained in earlier iterations.",
        "The loop stops when the generated reasoning expresses an answer or when the maximum number of iterations is reached.",
        "The evaluation covers four knowledge-intensive multi-step question-answering datasets.",
        "Interleaving reasoning and retrieval substantially improves fixed-budget evidence recall over one-step retrieval.",
        "Higher retrieval recall usually translates into improved question-answering performance but not in every dataset.",
        "The authors observe fewer factual errors in reasoning when retrieval is interleaved with the chain of thought.",
        "Retrieval gains remain visible with smaller language models even when their final QA gains are weaker.",
        "The authors released code, data-related resources, and prompting materials for the experiments."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2212.10509",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2112.08558",
      "title": "CONQRR: Conversational Query Rewriting for Retrieval with Reinforcement Learning",
      "research_question": "Can conversational query rewriting trained directly against retrieval rewards produce better standalone search queries for fixed off-the-shelf retrievers than supervised rewriting trained only to imitate human rewrites?",
      "methodology": "CONQRR uses a T5-base sequence-to-sequence model to rewrite the current conversational question and its dialogue context into a standalone retrieval query while leaving the downstream retriever fixed. Weak supervision identifies a likely positive passage from BM25 candidates by overlap with the known answer, and self-critical reinforcement learning rewards sampled rewrites when they rank that positive passage better than the model's greedy rewrite among training candidates; the paper studies both pure RL and a mixed RL-plus-cross-entropy objective. At inference, the model greedily generates one rewritten query, which is issued to either BM25 or a fixed T5-base dual-encoder retriever. Experiments use QReCC for training and in-domain testing, TREC conversational data for out-of-domain analysis, and MRR, Recall@10, and Recall@100 as retrieval metrics.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "On the updated QReCC BM25 evaluation, the pure-RL CONQRR model achieved MRR 0.383 and Recall@10 60.1 versus 0.328 and 52.5 for the supervised T5QR baseline; the mixed objective also outperformed T5QR.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The mixed CONQRR model outperformed supervised T5QR across the reported combinations of two fixed retrievers and the principal in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations, although individual metric differences on TREC can be small.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Retriever and Domain Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "With the dual-encoder retriever on the aggregate QReCC evaluation, pure-RL CONQRR reached MRR 0.418, Recall@10 0.651, and Recall@100 0.847, compared with 0.361, 0.562, and 0.759 for supervised T5QR.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Directly submitting the full dialogue context can work very well when a conversation remains centered on one topic but degrades sharply after topic shifts, while learned query rewriting is substantially more robust to those shifts.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Topic Shift Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "In an error analysis of 50 cases where mixed CONQRR underperformed the human rewrite with the dual encoder, the generated queries were fluent, but 56% omitted useful context and 34% introduced extra information associated with misinterpretation.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Error Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "CONQRR performs a single context-conditioned rewrite followed by retrieval; it does not inspect retrieved evidence and iteratively decide what evidence gap to query next or when evidence collection is complete.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Method"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "For conversations that remain strongly topic-concentrated, the raw dialogue context itself can already be an effective retrieval query, reducing the benefit of rewriting.",
        "The paper focuses on alternating question-answer conversational structure and identifies richer discourse phenomena such as clarification as future work.",
        "Positive training passages are obtained through weak supervision from retrieval candidates and answer overlap, so the reward target can inherit candidate-retrieval and labeling errors.",
        "The updated evaluation excludes examples for which a valid gold passage label cannot be established, substantially reducing the evaluated test set relative to the original data.",
        "Only two off-the-shelf retriever types are experimentally demonstrated, so claims of adaptation to arbitrary retrievers extend beyond the directly tested systems.",
        "The approach generates one retrieval query rather than running an evidence-aware multi-round retrieval loop with an explicit sufficiency or stopping decision.",
        "Permissions, document versions, source freshness, temporal validity, and cost-aware evidence acquisition are outside the evaluated problem formulation."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "retrieval_gain_over_supervised_rewriting": 0.99,
        "two_retriever_effectiveness": 0.98,
        "topic_shift_robustness": 0.98,
        "error_modes": 0.97,
        "single_step_not_iterative": 0.99,
        "arbitrary_retriever_generalization": 0.84
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "CONQRR rewrites a context-dependent conversational question into a standalone query for a fixed retriever.",
        "Its reinforcement-learning objective rewards rewrites according to retrieval performance rather than only similarity to a human-authored rewrite.",
        "Training uses weakly identified positive passages derived from answer overlap with retrieved candidates.",
        "The model uses self-critical training by comparing a sampled rewrite against its greedy rewrite.",
        "The paper evaluates both BM25 and a fixed neural dual-encoder retriever.",
        "CONQRR improves retrieval over a supervised T5 query-rewriting baseline on the main QReCC evaluations.",
        "Query rewriting is especially useful when the conversation changes topic and old dialogue turns become distracting.",
        "Raw dialogue context can be highly competitive when the conversation remains concentrated on the same topic.",
        "Error analysis finds both missing-context and added-misinterpretation failures in generated rewrites.",
        "The method does not use retrieval feedback to generate additional queries after the initial rewrite."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2112.08558",
      "access": "full_text"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
